message: NFR-1 (<150ms glass-to-glass) will NOT be met by v1. Accepted at the clarify gate: v1 ships screenshot polling behind a MirrorTransport interface, with scrcpy-server + in-JVM H.264 decode as an explicit v1.1+ follow-up. Grounds: no H.264 decoder exists anywhere on the classpath (verified against gradle/libs.versions.toml), building one is disproportionate to this deliverable, and the staged interface makes the real transport a drop-in replacement. Deliberate, not an oversight. MUST appear in the final chain report to the operator.

Brainstorm surfaced a pre-existing repo gap it correctly did NOT silently patch: domain-usecase-impl resultLauncher catches Throwable, which includes CancellationException, so any coroutine timeout inside a use case must use withTimeoutOrNull rather than withTimeout or real cancellation gets swallowed and mapped to a Failure. Affects every existing use case, not just this spec. Carried as a follow-up for the batched retrospective.

Merged the sequence and validate steps into ONE agent call instead of two. Both read the same backlog and the validator must re-read the dependency graph anyway to check coverage, so splitting them pays two full context loads for one body of analysis. Budget-driven: F-1 consumed ~1.65M agent tokens end-to-end and 8.5 specs remain against ~14.8M, which leaves no margin at that rate. The combined agent is briefed to do BOTH jobs explicitly - cycle detection, topological waves, scope-disjointness verification file-by-file, AND coverage/well-formedness validation - so no check is dropped, only a context reload. Will apply to the remaining specs in the chain.

Pre-execution baseline on branch sdd/android-device-discovery-mirroring: the four-module desktop regression inherited from F-1 is green before any F-2 code lands. Any later failure is attributable to this spec.

Grouping the 8 waves into 4 worktree batches by layer rather than one worktree per wave: B1 = T-1,T-2,T-3 (domain-core vocabulary + data-device-api + its no-phone test suite), B2 = T-4,T-5,T-6,T-7 (data-device-impl ProcessBuilder + repository + poller + domain use cases), B3 = T-9,T-10 (presentation-core-ui RadioMark/SourceListRow + the 27 localisation keys - both independent of the data layer, so this batch runs IN PARALLEL with B2), B4 = T-8,T-11,T-12,T-13,T-14 (Koin wiring, the Orbit feature module, the measurement gate, its tests, and making the shell slots live). T-15 verification sweep and T-16 docs run last. Rationale: five of the eight waves are single-task and strictly sequential, so one agent per wave pays a full context reload to write a few files that the next agent immediately needs to re-read. Batching by layer keeps each agent inside one coherent body of work. Dependency order is preserved INSIDE each batch and ACROSS batches; per-task reports and status are still emitted separately so Stage 5 traceability is unaffected.

Every fresh git worktree lacks local.properties (correctly gitignored), so every gradle invocation inside one fails with SDK location not found until it is copied in. The B1 agent hit this and worked around it locally. Fixed centrally: worktrees are now created through a helper that seeds local.properties from the main checkout immediately after creation. Worth noting this is a gap in sdd.py worktree add itself - it creates a tree Gradle cannot build in - and is a candidate improvement for the batched retrospective.

T-9 shipped NoSignalStage with StageSurface geometry 180x380dp because the task mandated porting it verbatim, but comp 02 measures the phone outline at roughly 274x578dp. The agent followed the task over the comp and flagged it rather than silently picking one. NoSignalStage IS the stage content now, so the comp is arguably the authority. Two further items from the same report: the CTA ships at 32dp against the comp roughly 39dp because PageCta is the largest AppButtonSize tier that exists, and TAC8 could not be discharged by rendered comparison since this repo has no Compose UI-test or screenshot harness. All three go to Stage 5 for adjudication.

Stage 5 gate answered autonomously, all three taking the recommended option. Q1 fix-then-close: AF-1 and AF-2 are fixed as a change request before F-2 closes, not carried to F-3. AF-1 matters most - ScreencapMirrorTransport sets latencyMs = captureMs unconditionally, so the status bar would print a host-side capture round-trip labelled latency while StatsFormatter placeholder branch sits dead. That breaks precisely the honesty the NFR-1 waiver was granted on, so carrying it would be carrying a lie the waiver was supposed to prevent. AF-2: the iOS dot is a hardcoded constant although ToolKind.Idb, the non-SDK probeCandidates branch and ToolResolver all already ship and are unit-tested - one datasource member and one call are missing, and MirrorContent carries a comment claiming iOS IS probed, which is false. Q2 yes: AF-3 is fixed in the same change request - Key.Escape appears nowhere in the repo and ClosePicker is dispatched only from tests, so the picker is a one-way door and the only A11Y row in the plan is entirely unimplemented. Q3 design pass: the comp deltas (180x380 outline vs roughly 274x578, 32dp CTA vs roughly 39dp) route to a separate design-system ticket rather than being re-cut inside F-2.
